question.leadin: This leader was assassinated by Nathuram Godse [God-say] in 1948.
question.text: Name this central figure of India's independence movement who was given the honorific "Mahatma," or "Great Soul."
question.clue: With Lord Irwin, this person ended the salt tax in exchange for ending the Salt March.

swap.text: When she declared a state of emergency, Indira Gandhi and her son Sanjay spearheaded a population control strategy in which poor men and women were forced to undergo this medical procedure.
swap.answerHtml: sexual sterilization (accept word forms like sterilize; accept male and/or female sterilization; accept vasectomy or tubectomy)

question.text: A notable example of Mughul architecture is this white-domed mausoleum in Agra, built by Akbar's grandson Shah Jahan for his wife.
question.clue: This building's mausoleum has a reverberation time of 28 seconds, so that prayers conducted by the hafiz from the Quran would linger as long as possible.

swap.text: The Mughal dynasty was founded by this man, who conquered much of Northern India after the Battle of Panipat in 1526.
swap.clue: Rana Sanga of Mewar ("MAY-ver") was poisoned by his own Rajputs to prevent a second conflict with this ruler, the first of which ended at the Battle of Khanwa.

question.leadin: Name the following about the Chola [t'SHO-rah] Empire.
question.text: The Chola dynasty was of this ethnic group. This ethnic group's namesake tigers committed terrorist attacks in modern-day Sri Lanka.
question.clue: This ethnic group created "singing steps" leading up to one of their three "Great Living" temples; that temple depicted legends associated with 63 "poet-saints" of this ethnicity.

swap.text: This foreign leader ordered the RAW ["R-A-W"] to help train and arm Bangladeshi insurgents. The assassination of this Indian leader led to the launch of Operation Blue Star.
swap.clue: This leader ordered air strikes in response to Operation Chingiz Khan to support a "Liberation War" against a 1971 genocide launched by Operation Searchlight.

question.leadin: Answer the following about national leaders following successful independence movements.
question.text: Tajuddin Ahmad served as this nation's first Prime Minister after rising to power through his party, the Awami League. It broke away from Pakistan in 1971 to form a new nation with capital Dhaka.
question.clue: The Blood Telegram reported genocidal attacks carried out in this country on the orders of Yahya Khan during Operation Searchlight.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the geography of Adam's Bridge.
swap.text: This ethnic group partially names an Indian state next to Adam's Bridge. Velupillai Prabhakaran led a breakaway movement of these people until his 2009 death.
swap.clue: A kingdom of this people expanded its influence into SE Asia after raiding ports like Kedah and Palembang of the Srivijaya Kingdom.

question.text: This ruling Indian party is committed to Hindutva, or Hindu nationalism. This party, led by Narendra Modi, played a role in the destruction of the Babri Mosque in Ayodhya.
question.clue: Modi is a member of this right-wing party, which previously led the country from 1998-2004 as part of the National Democratic Alliance.

swap.text: The British moved from indirect to direct rule in this colony following the 1857 Sepoy Rebellion.
swap.clue: Lord Curzon established this colony's North-West Frontier Province, whose western border was set at the Durand Line to settle the Great Game with Russia.

question.text: This soldier led the British forces at Plassey. He had earlier successfully taken and held Arcot through a siege by Chanda Sahib, an action that caused Pitt the Elder to describe him as the "heaven-born general."
question.clue: The definitive biography of this man is H.H. Dodwell's, which contrasts him to his French counterpart, Joseph Dupleix.

swap.leadin: One of these things in Lumbini described how a ruler visited the city 20 years into his reign and abolished taxes there.
swap.text: Name this collection of over thirty inscriptions that encourage right behavior and kindness towards animals and others. These inscriptions were created in response to the violence of the Kalinga War.
swap.answerHtml: edicts of Ashoka [accept pillar edicts of Ashoka, accept rock edicts of Ashoka, accept pillars of Ashoka, accept pillars of Dharma, prompt on partial answers]
swap.clue: These documents outline a policy of proselytism towards the neighboring king Antiochus I, though they promote tolerance of all religions.

question.leadin: A monarch of this kingdom, Rajendra I, sent a military expedition to bring the water of the Ganges back to its capital.
question.text: Name this kingdom in Southern India that at its height extended its rule to the Malay peninsula. This kingdom was defeated by the Pandyas in the 13th century.
question.clue: Similar theories about the occupation of Northern India often propose that survivors of the Indus Valley Civilization fled South to establish three kingdoms in the Deccan: Chera, Pandya, and this largest Tamil empire.

swap.text: The day after the mosque's invasion, protesters burned down this city's U.S. embassy. It replaced Karachi as Pakistan's capital in 1961.
swap.clue: Built in 1960, name this city that became the capital of a South Asian nation that split from India in 1947.

question.text: Both Harper and the UK House Foreign Affairs Committee cited the human rights violations of this Sri Lankan president who used heavy-handed tactics to end his country's long-running civil war.
question.clue: The Tamil Tigers were defeated in 2009 under the leadership of this President of Sri Lanka who suffered a shock defeat in the 2015 presidential election to Maithripala Sirisena.

question.text: Name this series of four wars ending in 1799. At the end, the British defeated Hyder Ali and Tippu Sultan and annexed much of their land.
question.clue: The second, which lasted from 1780-17884, was ended by the Treaty of Mangalore, and saw the defeat of Hyder Ali at Porto Nova and his subsequent death, leaving his kingdom to his son Tipu Sultan, who fought against Cornwallis.

swap.leadin: This man dispatched the Younghusband expedition to Lhasa to establish a British presence in Tibet before the Russians could get there.
swap.text: Identify this successor of Lord Elgin as Viceroy of India.
swap.answerHtml: Lord Curzon [or George Nathaniel Curzon, Marquees Curzon or Baron Curzon of Kedleston or Earl Curzon of Kedleston]

question.leadin: This person's ideas are known today through a series of rock and pillar edicts, perhaps the most iconic of which has a top depicting four lions standing back to back.
question.text: Name the eventually pacifist emperor. He implemented a "conquest by dharma" policy and was the last strong ruler of the Mauryan Empire.
question.clue: Some monuments created by this man were inscribed in Brahmi, others were inscribed in Greek.

swap.leadin: This engagement pitted some turmeric-smeared forces on one side and Najib Khan's excellent defensive formations on the other.
swap.text: Name this 1761 battle in which the light Afghan cavalry led by Ahmad Durrani were finally able to overcome French-trained artillery commanded by Sadashivrao Bhau.
swap.clue: The offensive that led to this battle began when one side crossed the Jumna River and cut off their opponents' supply lines, forcing them to fight or starve.
